evals.name: Minimal Harness Creation
evals.prompt: I have a new TypeScript + React project with no agent setup. Create a minimal harness that makes my agent reliable for single-feature development.
evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md (~50-100 lines), feature_list.json with one bootstrap placeholder feature, init.sh with verification commands
expectations: AGENTS.md includes startup workflow (read files, run init, check feature list)
AGENTS.md includes one-feature-at-a-time policy
feature_list.json has valid JSON with id, name, description, status fields
init.sh runs install, type/static check, test, and build commands when available
All files are in project root directory

evals.name: Session Continuity Setup
evals.prompt: My agent forgets everything between sessions. I need persistent memory and session handoff so it can work on multi-day features.
evals.expected_output: progress.md template, session-handoff.md structure, memory directory setup instructions
expectations: progress.md includes sections: current state, what's done, what's in progress, blockers, next session should
session-handoff.md includes: what was accomplished, what remains, blockers/decisions, files modified
Instructions for memory directory creation (.claude/memory/ or similar)
Two-step save invariant explained (topic file then index)

evals.name: Harness Assessment
evals.prompt: I have an existing AGENTS.md file but my agent still breaks things. Assess my harness and tell me what to improve first.
evals.expected_output: Five-subsystem assessment with scores 1-5 for each, bottleneck identified, prioritized improvement plan
expectations: Assessment covers all 5 subsystems: Instructions, State, Verification, Scope, Lifecycle
Each subsystem scored 1-5 with justification
Lowest-scoring subsystem identified as bottleneck or candidate bottleneck
Prioritized improvement plan with 2-3 concrete next steps

evals.name: Verification Workflow Design
evals.prompt: My agent says 'done' but the tests fail. Design a verification workflow that forces the agent to actually verify before claiming completion.
evals.expected_output: Verification commands list, AGENTS.md section updates, optional quality score tracking
expectations: Explicit verification commands listed (tests, lint, type-check, build)
AGENTS.md includes Definition of Done section with verification requirement
End-of-session checklist includes verification evidence recording
Failure path says not to claim done when verification fails

evals.name: Memory Taxonomy Design
evals.prompt: I want my agent to remember project conventions and user preferences across sessions. Design a memory taxonomy and tell me what belongs where.
evals.expected_output: Memory layer definitions, type taxonomy for auto-memory, what to save vs what to skip
expectations: Instruction memory defined (human-curated, version-controlled)
Auto-memory defined (agent-written, persistent)
Type taxonomy with 3-4 types (e.g., user/feedback/project/reference)
Clear guidance on what NOT to save (derivable content)

evals.name: Tool Safety Design
evals.prompt: My custom coding agent can run shell commands and edit files. Design the tool registry and permission harness so it is powerful but does not silently do dangerous things.
evals.expected_output: Tool registry policy with per-call concurrency classification, default permissions, denial handling, and audit trail
expectations: Sensitive tools default to ask or deny instead of allow
Concurrency safety is classified per call rather than per tool
Permission evaluation side effects are acknowledged and not cached unsafely
Audit trail records command, decision, and reason

evals.name: Context Budget Plan
evals.prompt: My agent loads too many docs at startup and gets slow. Design a context strategy that keeps important context while controlling token cost.
evals.expected_output: Progressive disclosure plan using select/write/compress/isolate operations and explicit context budgets
expectations: Defines always-loaded metadata versus on-demand references
Uses SELECT, WRITE, COMPRESS, and ISOLATE operations
Includes hard caps or budget thresholds
Explains invalidation for memoized context builders

evals.name: Multi-Agent Coordination
evals.prompt: I want multiple agents to work on a large refactor without stepping on each other. Design a multi-agent harness and rules for delegation.
evals.expected_output: Coordinator/delegation design with ownership boundaries, context sharing policy, and merge/review gates
expectations: Defines coordinator, worker, and optional reviewer responsibilities
Assigns disjoint file or module ownership
Prevents recursive fork children from forking again
Includes integration and verification gate before claiming done

evals.name: Lifecycle Bootstrap
evals.prompt: Every new session starts inconsistently. Design startup, hook, and handoff lifecycle rules so a new agent can resume safely.
evals.expected_output: Lifecycle bootstrap design with init.sh, clean-state checks, handoff reads, and hook trust boundaries
expectations: init.sh is the standard startup and verification entrypoint
Startup reads AGENTS.md, feature_list.json, progress.md, and handoff when present
End-of-session procedure records evidence, blockers, and next step
Hooks are gated by trust and failure behavior is explicit

evals.name: Scripted Harness Validation
evals.prompt: Use the hbtl-harness-creator scripts to scaffold a harness, validate it, and produce an HTML assessment report for a repository.
evals.expected_output: Commands using create-harness.mjs, validate-harness.mjs, and render-assessment-html.mjs plus interpretation of score
expectations: Uses create-harness.mjs with a target directory
Uses validate-harness.mjs and explains five-subsystem score output
Uses render-assessment-html.mjs or run-benchmark.mjs with --html
Explains that structural benchmark complements but does not replace real before/after agent sessions

evals.name: Structured Planning Clarification
evals.prompt: Create a harness for a product team whose planning subagent currently sends users raw clarification questions. The client supports AskUserQuestion forms, and the planner must remain resumable across multiple clarification rounds.
evals.expected_output: Generated agent instructions use an elicitationForm handoff, AskUserQuestion rendering, structured answer accumulation, and same-subagent resume
expectations: Planning subagent returns elicitationForm.questions instead of raw openQuestions
Each question includes question, concise header, 2-4 described options, and explicit multiSelect
Main agent accumulates the complete answer set before resuming the same subagent once
Answers shape the resulting plan and tasks without persisting or reproducing raw Q&A

evals.name: Client-Sized Elicitation Batching
evals.prompt: Design the planning clarification workflow for a harness where the planner may return seven related questions but the active agent client accepts only three questions per AskUserQuestion call.
evals.expected_output: Client-neutral form with ordered coordinator batching, normalized accumulated answers, and one planner resume
expectations: elicitationForm itself has no question-count limit
Coordinator partitions questions in original order according to the active client limit
All batch answers are accumulated before a single planner resume
A declined batch keeps partial answers only in active session context and leaves remaining questions pending

evals.name: Elicitation Fallback and Validation
evals.prompt: Create planning-harness rules that still collect structured clarification when AskUserQuestion is unavailable, and prevent malformed subagent forms from being dumped into chat.
evals.expected_output: Equivalent Markdown fallback plus form validation and repair behavior
expectations: Markdown fallback preserves headers, options, descriptions, multi-select behavior, and custom answers
Malformed forms are returned to the same subagent with validation feedback
Malformed or raw questions are never exposed directly to the user
Single/custom answers normalize to strings and multi-select answers to string arrays

evals.name: Planner alias and resume identity
evals.prompt: Scaffold a harness whose planning phase uses a resumable subagent across multiple elicitation rounds. The engineer uses Cursor with Task-tool subagents.
evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md documents harness-planner / Hubtel Harness Planner as the visible alias, subagent ID as the resume handle, and prompt fallback when no display-name field exists
expectations: Planning subagent is dispatched with stable alias harness-planner or Hubtel Harness Planner when the client supports visible naming
Resume and elicitation continuation use the subagent ID captured on initial dispatch, not the alias
Graceful fallback documents Role: harness-planner prompt preamble when the spawn tool has no description parameter
Transient elicitation, client-sized batching, and same-subagent-once resume behavior remain unchanged

evals.name: Implementation-ready task description density
evals.prompt: During triage, the planning subagent has authored the full template-shaped Azure task descriptions for a multi-task feature (via get_harness_task_structure) and returned them with acceptance criteria. Validate them before harness_create_tasks.
evals.expected_output: Each description is template-shaped Markdown with dense Summary, Objectives, Regression Risks, Test Plan, and Technical Notes — not pointers to plan files — and the density bar holds for every task, not just the first few
expectations: Descriptions are authored by the planning subagent (feature-by-feature), not by the main agent in one trailing pass; the main agent validates rather than re-authors
Each description is submitted as HTML (h3/h4 headers, p, ul/li, code, pre/code), not raw Markdown, since Azure renders the description as HTML
Summary is 2-4 sentences covering what changes, product/user why, and delivered artifact shape
Objectives are action-verb-led verifiable outcomes, not title restatements
Regression Risks name concrete risks and how each stays contained
Test Plan maps to real scenarios and ties to requiredTests and verification
Technical Notes list applicable MCP tools, doc IDs, dependencies, or ordering caveats when non-obvious

evals.name: No task-description drift at scale (multi-feature)
evals.prompt: A large request decomposes into ~10 features and ~40 tasks across DB, API, UI, and pure-util layers. The planning subagent authors all Azure task descriptions feature-by-feature and returns them. Run the pre-creation self-audit gate across ALL features before calling harness_create_tasks once for every task.
evals.expected_output: Every task's description — including the last feature's tasks — is a bespoke, layer-appropriate implementation contract; no repeated boilerplate, no plan-pointers, no verb-stripped Objectives; the self-audit gate resumes the subagent to re-author any drift rather than shipping it
expectations: The planning subagent authors descriptions feature-by-feature (chunked), never the main agent in a single pass over all ~40 tasks
Every description is valid HTML (h3/h4, p, ul/li, code, pre/code) with no leftover raw Markdown (###, #### headings, - bullets, or triple-backtick fences)
The main agent runs the self-audit gate across all features before harness_create_tasks and only proceeds when every check passes
Cross-task dedup: no two tasks share an identical or trivially templated Summary, Objectives, Regression Risks, or Test Plan block
No description reduces its Implementation Guidelines or Technical Notes to a bare 'see .harness/plans/feat-NNN.md' pointer
No Objectives use a 'Deliver: <title-fragment>' verb-stripped or title-echo opener
No layer-mismatched boilerplate (e.g. 'Extend Drizzle schema' or 'defineApiHandler + zod' on a pure util or UI-only task)

The last feature's tasks clear the same Content bar as the first feature's; on any drift the main agent resumes the subagent (by subagent ID, context preserved) to re-author the offending feature's tasks
A single harness_create_tasks batch covers every task across every feature after the gate passes
